subject: Post-demo: performance checklist & regional routing decisions
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Kim <susan.kim@finquest.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: performance checklist & regional routing decisions

Hi Susan / FinQuest latency team,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — appreciate the detailed walk-through of the customer flows. Per our conversation I wanted to capture the performance and residency items we discussed and surface a concrete pilot plan so we can align on next steps. High-level asks we heard from you:

- Latency targets: 95th percentile (text gen) ~< 120ms for US users, ~< 180ms for EU, and ~< 250ms for APAC (streaming tail 99th needs extra slack).
- Throughput/burst: steady-state 1k–1.5k requests/sec; expected peak bursts up to 3k rps during pulse events.
- Concurrency: ~200 simultaneous streaming sessions per region; typical session length 8–12s, avg chunk size 256 tokens.
- Data residency: EU-origin customer requests and associated logs must remain in EU; no customer input or unredacted logs can be exported out of eu-west-1 without explicit consent.

Proposed pilot (draft):
1) Stand up a dedicated EU routing lane: private VPC or dedicated tenancy for eu traffic, with model weights and logs pinned to eu-west and strict KMS separation.
2) Canary in US region first (100 rps for 48h), then EU canary (100 rps) — ramp to 500 rps then steady 1k.
3) Streaming validation: run a streaming harness (gRPC/HTTP2) with recorded traffic to measure 99th and tail latencies; we will instrument KV cache reuse to mirror production behavior.
4) Failover policy: prefer region-first routing; fallback order EU -> US (same continent fallback) -> APAC only if capacity constraints and customer permits.

Attachments: redwood-routing-playbook.pdf (pilot playbook + routing policy templates).

Next actions: can you confirm the EU residency constraint language above and share a small sample traffic capture (10k requests OR a tcpdump/recording) we can replay? Also confirm whether FinQuest legal needs a specific data flow diagram for procurement.

If that looks right I can sync Marcus (solutions) to build the test harness and Aditya will size a dedicated pilot estimate that we can include in the quote.

Thanks,
Chloe
Chloe Martin

From: Susan Kim <susan.kim@finquest.com>

Cc: Latency Eng <latency-eng@finquest.com>, Carlos Ortiz <carlos@finquest.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: performance checklist & regional routing decisions

Thanks Chloe — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side after chatting with Eng team: 

- Targets: we actually need 99th < 250ms for streaming completeness across US/EU; for non-streaming gen p95 targets you pulled match our expectations (US 120ms, EU 180ms).
- Throughput: 1.2k steady with 3.5k short bursts is more realistic for our marketing spikes.
- Concurrency: 275 streaming sessions in peak is the upper bound.
- Residency: EU requirement is strict — request bodies, derived embeddings, and event logs must remain in region. Tokenization / model weights can be mirrored but customer input cannot leave eu-west-1 unless anonymized and contractually allowed.

Procurement: need SOC2 Type II and a short data flow diagram (PII handling) to include in our vendor packet — procurement expects that within 7 business days.

I've attached our perf spreadsheet that shows traffic shape and sample traces — helpful for sizing. Also we can provide a 10k request compressed HAR from our staging environment next week.

Look forward to the pilot plan.

Best,
Susan
Susan Kim
Director, Platform Engineering — FinQuest
susan.kim@finquest.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 07:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-demo: performance checklist & regional routing decisions

Looping in Marcus for the test-harness and technical steps. Quick internal summary + action items for Redwood: 

1) EU private lane: propose a dedicated Private deployment (VPC) in eu-west-1 for FinQuest EU traffic. This satisfies residency and KMS separation requirements.
2) Pilot sizing (initial): reserve 2x A100s equivalent for steady 1.2k rps + autoscale headroom for 3.5k bursts. We will refine after runbook replay.
3) Streaming behavior: Marcus to implement KV-cache reuse and realistic chunking in harness; measure 50ms token latency delta for cold vs warm KV cache — report p50/p95/p99.
4) Routing policy: implement geo-by-client-ip (region-first) with explicit fallback rules and an annotation that prevents routing of EU-marked sessions outside eu-west.
5) Deliverables by next Tue: SOC2 snapshot, data flow diagram stub, pilot runbook, and a proposed canary schedule.

Marcus — can you confirm the harness timeline? I think 3 business days to build the replay harness if we get the HAR/traffic by Monday. Also add a small k6 script for burst simulation so FinQuest can run it locally.

Aditya
Sr. Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: performance checklist & regional routing decisions

Susan / team — thanks for the quick clarification and for the perf file. Updated plan below (concise SLO language for procurement + pilot steps). Please confirm by EOD Mon so we can lock resources: 

SLO language (proposed for procurement):
- For interactive non-streaming generation: p95 latency ≤ 120ms (US), ≤ 180ms (EU), ≤ 250ms (APAC).
- For streaming sessions: p99 tail latency ≤ 250ms across US/EU; APAC target to be treated as best-effort during pilot.
- Availability: 99.9% regionally for pinned capacity lanes (SLA during pilot is not final; to be negotiated in contract).

Pilot timeline & asks:
- Week 0: Redwood provides SOC2 snapshot and data-flow diagram (we will redact sensitive specifics) + routing playbook (attached).
- Week 1: FinQuest provides HAR or 10k compressed request capture.
- Week 2: Redwood runs canary replay in US (100 rps) and EU (100 rps), instruments metrics + KV cache warm runs, shares results + regression dashboard.
- Week 3: Ramp to 500rps and then steady 1.2k for 48h; stress test for 3.5k bursts for 30m.

Deliverables attached: redwood-routing-playbook.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf (snapshot).

If agreeable, I propose a short kickoff Wed 10am PT to confirm traffic handoff and legal items.

Thanks — will await confirmation and the HAR.

Chloe
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
